blocks.h2: Filtration Options for Hanover Park Homes

tiles.body: Very clean water from a dedicated faucet.

bodies: We test hardness, chlorine and sediment at your tap and explain the results plainly.

Hanover Park's water is Lake Michigan water, treated by the City of Chicago and delivered through a regional water agency. The village publishes a yearly water quality report. For health-related testing, a state-certified lab can run a full panel, and we'll point you to one.

blocks.intro: Under normal conditions, Hanover Park uses 100% Lake Michigan water.

items.body: Many people filter for chlorine taste or peace of mind.
The village keeps four wells for emergency use only.
A whole-house filter covers every tap. An under-sink filter covers drinking water.

blocks.h2: Which Filter Fits Your Hanover Park Home?
blocks.body: Start with the reason. If it's taste or chlorine smell in drinking water, an under-sink carbon filter or reverse osmosis system at the kitchen sink is usually enough. If you want filtered water at every faucet and shower, a whole-house filter goes on the main line where water enters the home. If scale on fixtures is the complaint, a test tells us whether a softener is worth it on Lake Michigan water. We'll match the system to the goal.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Filtration
blocks.body: Under-sink filters are the simplest. Reverse osmosis adds a tank and faucet. Whole-house systems go on the main line and need space nearby. Your household size and goals decide the equipment. We test first and quote a flat price.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: Where does Hanover Park's water come from?
items.answer: Under normal conditions, 100% Lake Michigan water, treated by the City of Chicago.

items.q: Do I need a water softener?
items.preview: It depends. We'll test your water first.
items.answer: Lake Michigan water is hard, but less hard than most well water. Some homes add a softener to cut scale, and many do fine without one. We'll test and tell you.
For better drinking water, under-sink. For every tap and shower, whole-house.

items.q: How often do filters need changing?
items.answer: Under-sink cartridges every several months. Whole-house filters vary.

items.q: Will a whole-house filter lower my water pressure?
items.answer: Not if it's sized for your home's flow. We size it so pressure stays steady.
Yes. Carbon filters reduce chlorine taste and odor.

items.answer: It depends on the system and installation. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we install.
